newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end mixed ahead of end-of-account.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end mixed ahead of end-of-account.

text.p: ** (1210 GMT) Profit-takers slice sharp early gains, halt
five-day rally in Indian shares
** Close of weekly account on Friday trigger unwinding of
positions-traders
** Benchmark Bombay share index closes 10.44 points lower at
4,323.46 -- after peaking at 4,393.29
** National exchange index sheds 6.55 points to 1,216.40
** Delhi share index ends 2.12 points higher at 912.47, off
918.55 high; Madras index drops 17.79 points to 4,356.10
and CRISIL-500 index loses 2.45 to 771.81
Shares across Indian exchanges closed mixed on Thursday as local players unwinded positions after a five-day rally, brokers said.
"This reaction was well anticipated," said Sunil Kothari at brokerage Nagindas S. Kothari. "A correction was due because the market had gone up too sharply."
Players were encouraged to cut exposures because Friday is the last day of the weekly account, he said.
"I expect more selling tomorrow," he said. "But, it could rebound if foreign funds come in aggressively."
Hopes of an economic upturn propelled by falling interest rates and easy money conditions are luring foreign funds into Indian equities, an international fund manager told Reuters.

"I think it's a good chance that you will see the economy starting to pick up in the second half. Some early signs are there, but nothing concrete," Nikhil Khattau, chief executive at SUN F&C Asset Management (I) Pvt Ltd.
The markets are discounting the longer-term gains. "I think we'll have to be slightly ahead of the herd," he said.
Analysts said foreign demand was restricted to blue-chip shares with the buying not spilling to the broader section.
"We're seeing buying from U.S. based index-funds," said fund manager S.M. Athalye, associate vice president (investments) at Tata Asset Management Ltd.
"The buying is only in index stocks," he said.
Software stock Infosys finished 20 rupees higher at 1,960, off 1,905.25 day's low, after the firm said its board will finalise first quarter financial results on July 7.
